Each item has id (ws_..., used as workspace_id by most tools), name, timezone, currency, plan, plan_events, subscription_status and role (the caller's role). Call sites_list with a workspace id next to find site ids. Creating a workspace is only possible in the app.

account_get.description: Returns the signed-in member's own profile and preferences. Use it to read settings before changing them with account_update. This is about the person, not a workspace. Workspace plan and invoices are under billing_get. Fields are email, unconfirmed_email (set while an email change awaits confirmation, otherwise null), name (nullable), theme (system, light or dark), default_landing (sites or last_site), locale (language code for the signed-in app), timezone (IANA name, nullable), shortcuts_enabled, reduce_motion, product_emails, site_audit_emails, marketing_emails, newsletter (all booleans where true means subscribed), two_factor (boolean), passkeys (count of registered passkeys) and created_at (ISO 8601). A session opened only through a workspace identity provider sees just email and the display settings.

webhooks_create.description: Adds an endpoint that receives POSTed JSON for workspace events (path takes workspace_id). url must be a public https address, private and internal addresses are refused. events is a required list chosen from alert.triggered, alert.resolved, goal.completed_threshold, uptime.down, uptime.up, export.ready, import.completed, import.failed, site.created, site.deleted, member.added, usage.threshold and site_audit.completed. enabled defaults to true. A signing secret (whsec_...) is generated and returned in the response, and each delivery carries a Privatus-Signature header with a timestamp and an HMAC-SHA256 of the body made with it. Failed deliveries are retried with backoff and the endpoint is disabled after 20 failures in a row. Use webhooks_test to send a sample.

sites_list.description: Lists the sites of a workspace that the caller can access, paginated, with the caller's starred sites first. The response meta has per-page pagination plus stats, an object keyed by site id with visitors (recent unique visitors), change (percent change against the previous period), sparkline (a list of daily values) and live (current visitors), totals across the page, and labels (every label of the sites the caller can access, sorted). Each item has the same fields as sites_get. This is the starting point for finding the site ids (pa_...) used by every other site tool. Requires analytics.read.

sites_create.description: Adds a website to a workspace and returns it, including the tracking snippet to install. The workspace's plan limits the number of sites (Free allows 3) and the call fails with a plan-limit error when it is reached. domain is required and is normalized (for example a full URL or www prefix is reduced to the hostname). name defaults to the domain, timezone defaults to the workspace's timezone (an IANA name such as Europe/Berlin) and currency to the workspace currency (a 3-letter ISO 4217 code such as USD). stats_aggregate.summary: Headline metrics for a period (with comparison)
stats_aggregate.description: Headline numbers for one period, as one object. Returns period {from, to} and metrics {visitors, visits, pageviews, views_per_visit, bounce_rate, visit_duration, revenue}. With compare it also returns comparison_period, comparison (the same metrics for the other range) and change (percent change per metric, null when the earlier value was 0). Units: bounce_rate is a percent from 0 to 100 (10.9 means 10.9%). visit_duration is the median engaged time of a visit in milliseconds. revenue is an integer in minor units (cents) of the site currency. views_per_visit is a decimal. Visitors are counted per day because no persistent visitor id is stored, so someone who comes back on another day counts again. Use this for totals and period-over-period change. Use stats_timeseries for a chart over time, stats_breakdown for top values of a dimension, and stats_overview for all of it in one call. Narrow any of them with filters (see filters for the dimension names and operators).

inputs.description: Site id, e.g. pa_7Q2K9XH3AB

inputs.description: First day of the range as YYYY-MM-DD, in the site's timezone. Only used when period is custom. Without it the range starts 29 days before to

inputs.name: to
inputs.description: Last day of the range as YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. Only used when period is custom. Without it the range ends today

inputs.description: First day of the comparison range as YYYY-MM-DD. Only used when compare is custom

inputs.name: compare_to
inputs.description: Last day of the comparison range as YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. Only used when compare is custom

inputs.name: match_weekday
inputs.description: Shift the comparison range so days of the week line up (Monday against Monday)

inputs.description: Filters that must all match: a list of [dimension, operator, value] conditions, e.g. [["country","is","US"],["page","starts_with","/blog"]]. Dimensions: channel, referrer, referrer_url, utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_content, utm_term, ref, hostname, country, language, device, browser, browser_version, os, os_version, screen, entry_page, exit_page, interaction, bot_score, page, event, goal, prop:<key>. Use the exact singular names (country, not countries). Values are as stored: country is a two-letter code such as US, channel is a name such as organic_search, a page is a path such as /pricing. Operators taking one value: is, is_not, contains, not_contains, starts_with, wildcard and not_wildcard (the value uses * as a wildcard, e.g. /blog/*), regex and not_regex (a Postgres regular expression of up to 200 characters), gt and lt (a number). any_of and none_of take a list: ["country","any_of",["US","DE"]]. between takes two numbers: ["prop:price","between",[10,50]]. For OR, wrap conditions in an object: {"any":[["channel","is","email"],["utm_medium","is","email"]]}. Up to 20 conditions.

inputs.description: Apply a saved segment by its id (seg_…, from segments_list). Its filters are added to filters

stats_breakdown.summary: Top values of a dimension (pages, sources, countries…)
stats_breakdown.description: Top values of one dimension with their metrics, most important first, paginated. The dimension is the last part of the path and must be an exact name from its description (for example country, page, channel, utm_campaign, prop:plan). Returns period, dimension, label, page, limit, has_more and rows. Ask for the next page while has_more is true. Every row has value and share (percent of the period total). The other fields of a row depend on the dimension. Visit dimensions (channel, referrer, referrer_url, utm_*, ref, hostname, country, language, device, browser, browser_version, os, os_version, screen, entry_page, exit_page, interaction, bot_score) give visitors, visits, pageviews, views_per_visit, bounce_rate, visit_duration and revenue. page gives pageviews, visits, time_on_page (milliseconds) and scroll_depth (percent), with no visitors. event and prop:<key> give completions, visits, revenue and conversion_rate. goal gives goal_id, completions, conversions, conversion_rate and revenue. Units: bounce_rate and conversion_rate are percents (0 to 100), durations are milliseconds, revenue is in minor units (cents). A wrong dimension returns a 422 that lists the valid names. Use search to look for a value across all rows, and filters to narrow the data first (for example pages visited by one country). For one page or one referrer in depth use pages_detail or referrers_detail. The interaction and bot_score dimensions need the Business or Enterprise plan: as a breakdown they respond with 402 plan_limit on other plans, and a filter on one is left out.

live_get.summary: Live visitors, activity stream and what is popular right now (last 30 minutes)
live_get.description: What is happening on the site right now. Returns live_visitors (visitors in the last 5 minutes), window_minutes (30), sparkline (visits per minute for the last 30 minutes, oldest first, each {minute, visits}), feed (the latest activity), top_pages, top_referrers, top_countries (each up to 8 rows of {value, visits}), countries (every country with a visit, same shape, for the map) and top_events (up to 8 of {value, completions}) for the last 30 minutes. feed entries have occurred_at, kind, name, path, channel, referrer_host, country, device and browser. They are anonymous, with no IP, city or visitor trail. feed shows all hits by default, or only pageviews or events, with limit entries (default 50, up to the buffer size of 100). The numbers are not cached and take no period. Pass filters (same format as stats_aggregate) to narrow every number and the feed to the matching hits. exports_create.description: Queues a data export that is built in the background and returns it right away with status queued. Choose it when you need a file (CSV, JSON, XLSX, NDJSON or a ZIP of dashboard panels), and use exports_preview first to check columns and size without creating anything. For lightweight numbers use the stats tools instead. Required inputs are workspace_id (path), site_id, from and to (YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive, in the export timezone). The kind decides what is exported and which options apply. aggregated (default) gives visit metrics per time bucket and uses grouping, dimensions (up to 6), metrics, filters and segment_id. pageviews, events and raw give one row per hit and use fields, filters and segment_id, require the Pro plan or above, and are limited to 400 days (raw to 93 days). imported gives imported daily stats and uses only dimensions. dashboard gives a ZIP of the overview panels (format zip only). Allowed file_format per kind is csv, json or xlsx for aggregated, pageviews, events and imported, csv or ndjson for raw, and zip for dashboard. Options that do not apply to the chosen kind are ignored. A workspace can have at most 5 exports queued or running at once. The response is the export with id (exp_...), status, row_count and expires_at (null until built). Poll exports_get until status is complete, then call exports_download. The requesting user gets an email when it is ready, a webhook export.ready is sent, and the action is written to the audit log. Event properties in the props column only include properties marked as safe to export (see event_properties_list).
